note: crate root
one error enum for the store; the Java throws IndexAlreadyExistsException, NameBeingReclaimedException, IllegalArgumentException and IOException
validateIndexOrAlias and validatePrefix with their messages; an unpaired surrogate cannot occur in a Rust string
create, get, resolve, resolveRaw, generationOf, update, delete, deleteIfUnchanged, createAlias, updateAlias (createRegister shared); recordChangesIn, changed and aboutToDelete; onChanged
honoured; the second writer is a plain PUT of the next generation the store does not remember, where the Java uses a second container

one ordered walk over the markers that stops at the first young hour, where the Java lists the bucket directory then each bucket; claims are deleted one at a time rather than batched; a malformed tombstone is kept rather than failing the sweep
listPage (DescriptorPage becomes the returned cursor) and namesWithPrefix (TooManyMatchesException becomes MetaError::TooManyMatches); serial reads, no listAll
bump (read and swap, 64 attempts) and read; Snapshot.unchangedSince; refuses names over 255 bytes or with a newline, which the Java does not
read and update (10 attempts, no pause); firstListValue and flatten are REST helpers and come with the handlers

createAlias, updateAlias (three-argument), deleteAlias (with generation), detachFromAliases, recoverAlias, resolveForAliasMutation, aliasesOf, prepare and remove hints; prepares only the members a change adds, where the Java reads every member; refuses an update that renames; the wait counts its pauses where the Java reads a clock; detachFromAliases returns how many aliases kept changing where the Java logs, and counts an alias left alone (the last index, or no longer a member) as done; no digest rollup mark yet

resolveForRouting, forgetRouting, prune and setters; keeps register bytes and parses on a hit where the Java keeps the parsed record; a read past the budget evicts only expired entries where the Java's cache evicts least recently used; readConfirmingIncarnation comes with the write fences

createIndex, deleteIndex (with and without the expected uuid), reclaim; a create refused for a name holding the same uuid answers its generation (a retry after a lost response); returns what the delete left (aliases still naming it, shards pinned or not cleared) where the Java logs

enqueue, drain, setDelayMillis; one ordered walk that stops at the first bucket not yet due and resumes past another node's bucket at a page end, where the Java lists the bucket directory then each bucket; a taken intent is deleted one at a time rather than batched; a failed GET keeps it, an unreadable body drops it, as the Java

purgeShardData; heads (ShardHeadStore readAllOf, deleteIfUnchanged, releaseAllOf, deleteAllOf) and pins (pinnedBy, pinnedByView) are traits with no implementation until the writer's heads and snapshots are ported
create, finish, extend, read, release, expire, live and reap over the state register and inventory marker, with legacy adoption
expire, live and reap, with the inventory listing
freeze: the capture marker, the incarnation check, each shard manifest, the finished view
put, get, delete, all (for_each) and names over the indexed marker; no legacy form, no node cache, no prefix selection; content keys are random ids, not hashes
TemplateCache and TemplateStore.all as one snapshot; currency also compares names and keys; no per-revision content cache
describeRepository, listRepositories, and SnapshotStore.state: read-only
putRepository and deleteRepository, with SnapshotStore.list as the in-use check
create, finish and remove: the reservation, protective marker, finish and cleanup of a take
deleteSnapshot for a shallow snapshot: release the name's register, then remove the marker; a standard snapshot is refused (its data prefix needs a LIST)
capture: describing an index and reading each shard commit
restore of one index of a shallow snapshot: create the descriptor, copy each captured file into the first-term container, land the manifest from absent (SnapshotBlobs.copyShardBlobs)
a captured range of one blob as a PUT body (SnapshotBlobs.copyShardBlobs)
restore of one index of a stock OpenSearch snapshot: the descriptor, then each shard's files copied whole from the source repository with the footer CRC checked; the shell has no such path
export of one shard's committed files into a stock repository as whole blobs, measured as they stream; the shell has no such path
publishing an exported snapshot into a stock repository: blobs, then index-N by conditional create with adoption of a winner, then index.latest; the shell has no such path
the fence of an export: the next index-N by conditional create, the adoption of a winner, then index.latest; the shell has no such path
reading a stock repository's index.latest, index-N, snapshot, metadata and shard blobs through a source store by derived keys, bounded; no Java counterpart in the shell
the four read rounds and every refusal and bound of a stock restore before any write; no Java counterpart in the shell
one blob read for each item, at most a fan-out at a time; no Java counterpart in the shell
tests of the unmarking after a restore; the shell tests restore end to end
one alias mutation adding a restore's members (ADR 0065); the Java shell makes the matching change on its own branch
the take's confirm of each index's aliases (ADR 0065); the Java shell makes the matching change on its own branch
registration, removal and slot claims over the registry registers (alerting spec, slice 1); no Java counterpart
a tenant's monitors over the index register and the registry (alerting spec, slice 2); no Java counterpart
update: a change rebuilt from the current document on every swap attempt; the Java has no read-modify-write set change
a monitor's alert register read and changed by compare-and-swap (alerting spec, slice 6); no Java counterpart
